export const meta = {
  name: 'phase1-review-fixes',
  description: 'Fix the 10 confirmed Phase 1 review findings (two disjoint agents), then verify',
  phases: [{ title: 'Fix', detail: 'runtime/model-layer agent || sandbox/schema agent' }, { title: 'Verify', detail: 'full suite + review tests + adversarial diff check' }],
}
const COMMON = `Repo /home/user/workflow-foundry (Node 24.21 on PATH; node:test; do NOT git commit; do NOT add npm deps). An adversarial review wrote tests/review-phase1.test.mjs with 10 failing tests (one per confirmed finding). Your job: make YOUR findings' tests pass by fixing PRODUCT code, never by weakening a test (only fix a review test if it is itself wrong, and say exactly why). Spec: research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md. Another agent is fixing other findings in parallel in OTHER files: edit only the files listed for you. Be surgical; keep the surrounding dense style. Run: node --test tests/review-phase1.test.mjs (your tests must pass) and the test files covering what you touch. Report every fix, test counts, rejected findings with reasons.`

const RUNTIME = `${COMMON}
You own: src/runtime.mjs, src/models/port.mjs, src/models/providers/claude-cli.mjs, src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs, src/journal.mjs, src/context.mjs, src/verdict.mjs, experiments/lib/services.mjs.
Findings:
2. MED port.mjs:194 + runtime.mjs:585-597 — cancelled model calls are journaled with their cost but never charged to run.cost/node cost. Carry journalId+cost on the CANCELLED error and charge before rethrow (dedupe by journalId as elsewhere).
3. MED runtime.mjs:676 oracle() — capability verifiers never charge cap.cost or check the budget; do it like task().
4. MED claude-cli.mjs:101 + port.mjs:168 — timed-out/killed hosted calls are journaled as exactly $0. Record costUnknown:true plus an upper bound (min of the per-call --max-budget-usd cap and an input-token list-price estimate); surface costUnknown/upper bound in journal costForRun and on node state/run (e.g. run.costUnknownUpperUsd) so experiments can report bounds. run.cost stays = known cost.
5. MED runtime.mjs:587/604 — a call cut short by the run deadline must be DEADLINE (inconclusive), not MODEL_TIMEOUT/CODE_TIMEOUT/TOOL_TIMEOUT.
6. MED port.mjs:37/130 — replay key must include a digest of the policy model entry + its provider config, and providers must resolve their own decoding defaults into the hashed decoding (e.g. llama max_tokens default 1024).
7. MED runtime.mjs:452/465, childLabels:250 — map failure:collect $error text from failed items must contribute the failed items' input/arg labels to the map output label.
9. LOW runtime.mjs:606 + context.mjs:105 — the E1 retry note embeds model-produced property names (steerable by untrusted input) outside the untrusted fence; render it inside a labelled block carrying the node's input label, or reduce it to schema paths only.
Also: experiments/lib/services.mjs uses runId 'gateway' for every session with seq restarting at 0; make the default runId unique per session (randomUUID).`

const SANDBOX = `${COMMON}
You own: src/schema-subset.mjs, src/sandbox.mjs (and tests/sandbox.test.mjs only to ADD tests).
Findings:
1. HIGH schema-subset.mjs:73 (quarantinedSchemaViolations) — quarantined schemas have unbounded output capacity (arrays of 1-char enums with maxItems 4096; arrays of floats), so untrusted text can be carried through and relabelled trusted. Fix: compute and cap total output capacity (about 64 bits: log2(enum size) per enum, log2(range+1) per bounded integer, booleans 1 bit, × maxItems for arrays; numbers must be integers with minimum and maximum, or rejected); require maxItems on arrays; reject strings that are not enums.
8. MED sandbox.mjs:87-88/102 — no effective memory/process limits: JS Buffers bypass --max-old-space-size, Python unlimited, fork possible. Apply prlimit (or setrlimit via the launcher) inside the namespace: address space ~1 GiB for python (JS: limit via --max-old-space-size plus an RLIMIT_AS compatible with V8, or RLIMIT_DATA), NPROC small, FSIZE small; keep all existing escape hardening intact.
10. LOW sandbox.mjs:11 MASKED_PATHS is a denylist: /mnt (uploads), /opt/corpus, /opt/claude-code are readable. Mask /mnt, every /opt subdirectory except the node runtime actually used (resolve from process.execPath, e.g. /opt/node24) , /home entirely, /srv, /media; if an allowlist root (pivot_root onto a minimal tree) is feasible within the existing design, prefer it.`

phase('Fix')
const [rt, sb] = await parallel([
  () => agent(RUNTIME, { label: 'fix:runtime+model-layer', phase: 'Fix' }),
  () => agent(SANDBOX, { label: 'fix:sandbox+schema', phase: 'Fix' }),
])
phase('Verify')
const verify = await agent(`Repo /home/user/workflow-foundry (Node 24). Two agents just fixed the Phase 1 review findings. Their reports:
--- runtime ---
${rt}
--- sandbox ---
${sb}
Do NOT edit files except to fix a clear regression the fixers introduced (say so). Run: node --test tests/review-phase1.test.mjs (expect 10/10 pass) and the full npm test (report exact tests/pass/fail/skip; the previous baseline was 735 tests, 718 pass, 0 fail, 17 skip plus the 10 review tests). Then adversarially re-read the diff (git diff) for: weakened tests, fixes that only special-case the test, broken replay determinism (do identical calls still produce identical replay keys across runs?), cost double-counting introduced by the cancel/charge changes, and sandbox hardening regressions. Report concrete problems with file:line, or 'no problems found'.`, { label: 'verify-fixes', phase: 'Verify' })
return { rt, sb, verify }

result.rt:
All 7 of my findings are fixed in product code. `tests/review-phase1.test.mjs` passes 10/10: my 7, plus the other agent's 3 (quarantine and the two sandbox tests). I did not edit any test and did not reject any finding.

I did not commit. Another session made a WIP snapshot commit (`b9d45c4`) that picked up my working-tree edits. My files have no uncommitted changes, and that commit holds my final versions.

**Fixes**

- **Finding 2, cancelled call cost** (`port.mjs`, `runtime.mjs`): the CANCELLED error now carries the journal id and the cost. The runtime charges it to the node and `run.cost` before rethrowing (event `model.cancelled`). Charging is shared with the normal path in a new `chargeModel()`, which still skips a journal id it has already charged.
- **Finding 3, verifier cost** (`runtime.mjs` `oracle()`): each dispatch now reserves `cap.cost` and checks the cost budget (event `oracle.dispatched`). I didn't reuse `checkBudget`, because the verify node has already taken its step and `checkBudget` would wrongly stop it on the step limit.
- **Finding 4, killed hosted call recorded as $0** (`claude-cli.mjs`, `port.mjs`, `journal.mjs`, `runtime.mjs`, `services.mjs`):
  - When the CLI ran but returned no result (timeout, cancel, output limit, crash), the provider marks the cost as unknown.
  - The journal row records `costUnknown: true`, `costUpperUsd` and `costEstimateUsd`.
  - `costForRun` adds `costUnknownCalls`, `costUnknownUpperUsd` (null if any call has no bound) and `costUnknownEstimateUsd`, only when such calls exist. This keeps the existing exact-shape test in `journal.test.mjs` passing.
  - Node state and the run get `costUnknownCalls` and `costUnknownUpperUsd`; the gateway ledger and `/budget` report the same. `run.cost` stays known cost only.
  - **One deliberate change from the brief:** `costUpperUsd` is the per-call `--max-budget-usd` cap, not min(cap, input estimate). An input-only estimate leaves out output tokens a killed call may already have been billed for, so it is not an upper bound. I record it separately as `costEstimateUsd` (capped). The cap itself is checked by the CLI between turns, so a single turn could go over it.
- **Finding 5, deadline vs timeout** (`runtime.mjs`):
  - Model calls and code now stop at the run deadline through their own abort signal (`untilDeadline()`), and a stop by that signal becomes DEADLINE.
  - A simpler "remaining time ≤ node timeout" check would have broken an existing test: a provider-reported instant `MODEL_TIMEOUT` (`runtime-agent` "outages" test) would have become DEADLINE.
  - Task and oracle timers belong to the runtime, so a timer set by the deadline throws DEADLINE there. A task never retries it or turns it into a handled error.
  - `verdict.mjs` needed no change: DEADLINE was already inconclusive.
- **Finding 6, replay key** (`port.mjs`, `llama-server.mjs`, `claude-cli.mjs`):
  - The key now includes a digest of the policy entry plus its provider config. Price and `imputedComputeUsdPerHour` are left out because they only affect accounting.
  - It also hashes the decoding the provider actually applies: llama defaults to max tokens 1024 and temperature 0; claude records effort, thinking tokens and "provider-default".
  - A provider instance resolves its own options through `effectiveDecoding`. When no provider is registered (CLI replay registers none), the standard resolver for that provider kind is used.
  - Those resolvers, and the THINKING/EFFORT tables, now live in `port.mjs`, with THINKING re-exported from `claude-cli.mjs`. Importing the provider modules from the port broke `tests/engine-binding.test.mjs`, which copies exactly the engine-identity file set. These tables decide replay keys, so they belong in that set anyway.
- **Finding 7, map collect label** (`runtime.mjs`): when any item failed, the map output label now joins every label the item frames could read (inputs and item).
- **Finding 9, E1 retry note** (`port.mjs`, `runtime.mjs`): the note now contains only schema paths and fixed text, never model-produced keys.
  - The port gives errors it generated itself a `feedback` field built from fixed text plus schema paths and schema-derived messages.
  - The runtime uses that field, or a fixed per-code text for errors reported by a provider.
  - `context.mjs` is unchanged, and the existing assertion on "Model output is not a JSON value" still passes.
- **`services.mjs`**: the default `runId` is now `gateway-<randomUUID()>` and is returned from `startServices`.

**Test counts (final)**
- Review: 10/10.
- Related suites, all passing: models-port 14, journal 5, runtime-agent 24, runtime-replay 5, runtime-map-parallel 13, runtime-code-verify 14, verdict 8, timers 9, ports 7, engine-binding 3, packaging 4 (+1 skipped), services 2, gateway 1.
- Full suite (`tests/*.test.mjs` + `experiments/lib/*.test.mjs`): 765 tests, 746 pass, 1 fail, 18 skipped. The failure is `tests/context.test.mjs:189` (quarantine schema), thrown from the other agent's `src/schema-subset.mjs` change.
- I also ran a throwaway scratchpad probe for paths the review tests don't cover; all passed. It checked run/node/journal unknown-cost fields, DEADLINE vs TOOL_TIMEOUT for tasks, DEADLINE vs CODE_TIMEOUT for code, an oracle cut off by the deadline, and llama replay with no provider registered.

**Follow-ups outside my files**
- `DESIGN.md` §3 (replay-key formula) and §4 (retry-note content) need updating to match.
- Journals recorded before this change no longer replay, because every replay key changed.
- `src/models/providers/gateway.mjs` ignores `costUnknown`/`costUpperUsd` in the host `/model` response, so a sandboxed run's own journal records those calls as known cost. The host journal and ledger have the correct values.

Files:
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/runtime.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/port.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/claude-cli.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/src/journal.mjs
- /home/user/workflow-foundry/experiments/lib/services.mjs
result.sb:
All three of my findings (1, 8, 10) are fixed and their review tests pass. One deviation from the brief: bounded floats are counted at their real capacity rather than rejected outright. One test in a file I don't own now fails because its fixture shows the bug that finding 1 forbids.

**Test counts**
- `node --test tests/review-phase1.test.mjs`: 10/10 pass, which includes the other agent's findings.
- `tests/sandbox.test.mjs`: 14/14 pass, including the 3 tests I added.
- Full suite (`node --test --test-concurrency=2 tests/*.test.mjs`): 754 tests, 734 pass, 2 fail, 18 skipped.
- I checked the 3 new sandbox tests against the original `src/sandbox.mjs` (from HEAD, in a scratch copy): all 3 fail there and pass on the new code.

**Fix 1 (HIGH), `src/schema-subset.mjs`**
- `quarantinedSchemaViolations` now adds up the total output capacity and rejects anything over the exported `QUARANTINE_MAX_BITS = 64`. It returns the violation `#: output capacity is N bits; a quarantined output may carry at most 64`.
- Bits per item:
  - boolean: 1
  - string enum: log2 of its distinct values
  - const: 0
  - integer: log2 of the integers in [min, max]
  - optional property: log2(values + 1), because whether it is present carries information
  - array: log2 of the possible lengths + maxItems × bits per item
- The existing rules stay: arrays need maxItems, free strings are rejected, objects need `additionalProperties: false`. The review case scores 26,922 bits and is rejected.
- **Deviation:** I did not reject non-integer numbers. They are charged at their exact capacity, which is log2 of the number of doubles in [min, max] (about 62 bits for [0, 1]). DESIGN §4 allows "bounded numbers/integers", and the JudgmentPort model engine in `src/ports.mjs:83` uses `confidence: number [0,1]` in a quarantined schema. Arrays of floats still fail: two floats come to 125.6 bits.
- **Not counted:** JSON key order. It is a channel of at most log2(k!) bits per object (k properties), and it would disappear if the runtime sorted the keys of declassified outputs.

**Fix 8 (MED), `src/sandbox.mjs`**
- The INNER script now runs `prlimit --pid $$` with soft = hard, before the READY line, so if prlimit is missing the run fails as `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`. The limits are in the exported `LIMITS`:
  - **Python:** address space 1 GiB, max processes 8, max file size 16 MiB, core 0.
  - **JS:** data limit 1.25 GiB, max processes 32, max file size 16 MiB, core 0, and `--max-old-space-size=512` is kept.
- Why JS needs a data limit rather than an address-space limit: Node crashes at startup with a 1 or 2 GiB address-space limit, and a 4 GiB one does not stop the 1 GiB Buffers. V8 also counts about 0.58 GiB of startup memory against the data limit, so at 1 GiB its 512 MiB heap could not be reached. At 1.25 GiB the heap reaches V8's own limit, and Buffers stop at about 700 MiB.
- **Root hosts now run the sandbox as uid/gid 65534.** The kernel never enforces the process limit for host root: under `--nproc=8`, 50 forks succeeded as root. As a side effect, sandboxed code no longer has owner access to root-owned files.

**Fix 10 (LOW), `src/sandbox.mjs`**
- I built the allowlist root rather than extending the denylist. Setup builds a fresh tmpfs containing only:
  - read-only binds of `VISIBLE_PATHS` (`/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/lib*`, and the `/etc/ld.so.*` and `localtime` entries)
  - the interpreter binary alone, at its own path (for example `/opt/node24/bin/node`)
  - `/proc`, five `/dev` nodes plus the fd links, and a private 16 MiB `/tmp`
- It then switches root onto it with `pivot_root`, detaches the host root and makes the new root read-only.
- `MASKED_PATHS` (`/home`, `/root`, `/opt`, `/mnt`, `/srv`, `/media`, `/tmp`, `/var`, `/run`) exist inside only as empty read-only directories.
- This also hides paths the old denylist left readable: `/sys`, `/nix`, `/boot`, `/old_root`, `/container_info.json` and nearly all of `/etc`.
- The two-level namespace, capability check, read-only remount loop, PATH-only environment and `--permission` are unchanged.
- Interpreters under `/tmp` are rejected. Interpreters under `/home` used to be rejected and are now allowed, with only the binary itself visible inside.

**Tests added to `tests/sandbox.test.mjs`**
- The root contains only allowlisted entries, the masked directories are empty, and `/tmp` is the only writable mount.
- The limits show in `/proc/self/limits`; a fork loop fails with BlockingIOError; 256 MiB allocates but 1 GiB raises MemoryError; JS can allocate 256 MiB of Buffers but not 1.5 GiB.
- On a root host, the sandboxed process's host uid is 65534.

**Cross-file consequences (not edited, not my files)**
1. `tests/context.test.mjs:190-192` now fails (full-suite #101). Its `ok` fixture has `n: { type:'number', minimum:-1, maximum:1 }`, which totals 78.1 bits and is the exact case finding 1 forbids. Fix: `n: { type:'integer', minimum:-1, maximum:1 }`, which brings it to about 17 bits.
2. In `src/ports.mjs:83`, the JudgmentPort model engine still works with up to 4 options (3 options is 63.6 bits). With 5 to 64 options it now fails `QUARANTINE_SCHEMA` at `compileContext`. I recommend changing `confidence` to an integer percent 0..100 and dividing by 100. `tests/ports.test.mjs` passes.
3. Full-suite #175 (engine-binding) fails because of the other agent's change: `src/models/port.mjs` now imports `providers/claude-cli.mjs` and `providers/llama-server.mjs`, which are not in the `src/engine.mjs:12` file list.
4. `research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md` §1.2 still describes the old tmpfs masks with no limits, and §4 has no capacity cap. Both are now out of date.
5. **Portability (all fail closed as `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` unless noted):**
   - The sandbox now needs the `pivot_root` and `prlimit` tools.
   - On root hosts, uid 65534 must be allowed to create user namespaces. Ubuntu's apparmor user-namespace restriction would block it.
   - The interpreter's shared libraries must be under `/usr` or `/lib`. A Nix-built Node would fail as `CODE_ERROR`, not `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`.
   - On non-root hosts the per-sandbox process limit needs Linux 5.14 or later; older kernels count all of the user's processes.

No findings rejected.
result.verify:
Two of the four checks hold up: replay keys stay deterministic and the cancel/charge changes don't double-count cost. There is one test failure in the full suite, one sandbox regression and three smaller latent problems; nothing found in your other categories. I edited no files. Another session's commit `65fe005` landed during the review but touches none of `src/`, `tests/` or `experiments/lib`, so these results still apply.

**Test results**
- `node --test tests/review-phase1.test.mjs`: 10 tests, 10 pass, 0 fail.
- `npm test` (`tests/*.test.mjs`): 754 tests, 735 pass, 1 fail, 18 skipped (0 cancelled, 0 todo).
  - The failure is `tests/context.test.mjs:189` ("schema subset: quarantine allows only booleans, string enums and bounded numbers"). Its `ok` fixture at lines 190-192 scores 78.1 bits and now throws `QUARANTINE_SCHEMA`.
  - Against the baseline (745 including the review tests) there are 9 more tests: 3 are the new sandbox tests and the rest come from other work. The extra skip is the live System One test, which needs `FOUNDRY_SYSTEMONE_URL`; neither fixer added it.
  - `tests/engine-binding` passes. The engine-binding failure the sandbox fixer reported is gone because the decoding tables moved into `port.mjs`.
- `experiments/lib/*.test.mjs`: 11 tests, 11 pass.

**Adversarial checks**
- **Weakened tests:** none. `tests/review-phase1.test.mjs` hasn't changed since `bfae6d4`. In `b9d45c4` the only test change is 45 added lines in `tests/sandbox.test.mjs`. `tests/context.test.mjs` is untouched, which is why it now fails.
- **Fixes that only special-case a test:** none found. Each fix changes the general mechanism rather than the case the test exercises.
- **Replay determinism:** identical calls still produce identical keys. I checked with a scratch probe using two separate ports and journals and a fixed salt, for both claude-cli and llama, with and without the provider's own decoding resolver. Retry-note feedback is stored in the journal row, so replay and crash recovery rebuild the same prompt. No journals are committed, so the change in every key strands nothing.
- **Cost double-counting:** none. `chargeModel` skips any journal id it has already charged, and CANCELLED rows are never replayed or recovered. A verify node is started with cost 0 (`src/runtime.mjs:388`), so the new oracle reservation is the only charge for the capability's cost. The cost total in `costForRun` is unchanged.

**Problems**
1. **Sandbox error misclassified (MED, regression), `src/sandbox.mjs:47-52` and `:122`.**
   - On a root host, sandbox setup now runs as uid 65534. If the interpreter sits in a directory that uid can't enter (for example `/root/.nvm/...`, since `/root` is mode 0700), the bind loop silently skips it. The READY line is still printed, then exec fails with exit 127.
   - The result is `CODE_ERROR`, which counts as the code's own failure, instead of `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`, which is an environment fault. Before the fix, `interpreter()` rejected `/root` paths as `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`.
   - Reproduced by copying node to a temporary directory under `/root` (since removed) and running `runCode`: `CODE_ERROR Code failed (exit 127): env: '/root/wf-sandbox-probe-28756/node': No such file or directory`.
   - Fix: after the loop, before READY, add `[ -e ".$2" ] || { echo "foundry-sandbox: interpreter $2 is not reachable" >&2; exit 96; }`.
2. **Floats nearly unusable under the capacity cap (MED), `src/schema-subset.mjs:72` and `:91`.**
   - A number in [0, 1] counts as about 62 bits, which leaves about 2 bits under the 64-bit cap.
   - This causes the red suite. It also breaks the JudgmentPort model engine (`src/ports.mjs:97`, enum choice plus a float confidence) for 5 or more options, which now throws `QUARANTINE_SCHEMA`.
   - The fixer's suggested change (making the fixture's `n` an integer) would turn the suite green but removes the only positive `type: number` case. Whether floats should be quantized, for example to an integer percent, is a decision for DESIGN §4, so I left it.
3. **Deadline timer can fire immediately (LOW, latent regression), `src/runtime.mjs:209`.**
   - `untilDeadline` passes `AbortSignal.timeout(deadline - now)` without a cap. Node clamps any delay above 2^31-1 ms (about 24.8 days) to 1 ms; I checked that a 2,591,999,000 ms timeout aborted after 3 ms.
   - The schema allows `maxDurationMs` up to 30 days, and `Runtime` accepts any positive policy value, so a longer host policy would make every model call and code node fail with DEADLINE at once.
   - The default cap is 1 hour and no host in the repo raises it.
   - Fix: wrap the delay in `Math.min(2 ** 31 - 1, …)`.
4. **Replay key depends on llama's max-tokens setting (LOW, latent), `src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs:22` and `src/models/port.mjs:60`.**
   - Live keys use the provider instance's `defaultMaxTokens`, but a replay with no provider registered (the CLI registers none, `bin/foundry.mjs:50-60`) always uses 1024.
   - A provider built with a different value records keys its own replay can't find. It fails closed as `REPLAY_MISS`. Nothing overrides the value today.
   - Separately, the key also covers fields that don't affect the model's output (`class`, `port`, `auth`, `knownGaps`), so editing documentation strings in the policy invalidates every journal.
5. **`/budget` hides an unbounded estimate (LOW), `experiments/lib/services.mjs:42`.**
   - `unknownUpperUsd: ledger.unknownUpperUsd ?? 0` turns the ledger's `null`, which means "no bound", into 0.
   - It can't happen yet because claude-cli always has a cap. Fix: map only `undefined` to 0.

**Remaining gaps (not regressions)**
- Unknown spend is only reported, never enforced. `run.cost` and the gateway's `spentUsd` exclude it, so repeated killed hosted calls (up to $1 each by default) never trigger either budget limit (`src/runtime.mjs:621`, `src/runtime.mjs:651`).
- The sandbox-side `GatewayProvider` ignores `costUnknown`, as the runtime fixer noted.
- DESIGN §1.2, §3 and §4 are out of date with these changes.

Files: `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/sandbox.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/schema-subset.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/ports.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/tests/context.test.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/runtime.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/port.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/src/models/providers/llama-server.mjs`, `/home/user/workflow-foundry/experiments/lib/services.mjs`
